rows.speaker: مجاهد وسعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: The goblets are continuously poured, an image drawn from repeatedly tightening the vessel while pouring.
rows.anchor: متتابعة على شاربيها أخذ من متابعة الشد في الدهق عن مجاهد وسعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra gives the goblets the gloss damādim, suggesting abundant pouring.
rows.anchor: وقيل: دمادم عن أبي هريرة

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says the drink is served according to the drinkers' thirst.
rows.anchor: على قدر ريهم عن مقاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of Paradise hear no idle, useless speech there.
rows.anchor: { لا يسمعون فيها } أي في الجنة { لغوا } أي كلاما لغوا لا فائدة فيه

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: On the light reading, the phrase means that they do not dispute or deny one another.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ بالتخفيف يريد ولا مكاذبة عن أبي عبيدة

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Abu Ali al-Farisi gives the alternative gloss falsehood for the word kadhiban.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كذبا عن أبي علي الفارسي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's treatment of the God-fearing is recompense for their belief in God and His Messenger.
rows.anchor: جزاء من ربك على تصديقهم بالله ونبيه

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة والجبائي
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda and al-Jubba'i explain his gift as sufficient for its recipients.
rows.anchor: { عطاء } أي أعطاهم الله عطاء { حسابا } أي كافيا عن أبي عبيدة والجبائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reported interpretation takes his gift to mean abundant.
rows.anchor: وقيل: حسابا أي كثيرا. وقيل:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes the gift proportionate to entitlement and deeds; al-Zajjaj says it suffices because it contains what they desire.
rows.anchor: وقيل: حسابا على قدر الاستحقاق وبحسب العمل قال الزجاج: معناه ما يكفيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who rewards believers is Lord and governor of the heavens, earth, and everything between them, acting as He wills; the Merciful bestows favors on believers and unbelievers.
rows.anchor: هو رب السماوات والأرض ومدبرهما ومدبر ما بينهما والمتصرف فيهما على ما يشاء الرحمن المنعم على خلقه مؤمنهم وكافرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one can address God or ask Him except in a matter for which He grants permission, as other verses also state.
rows.anchor: لا يملكون أن يسألوه إلا فيما أذن لهم فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khitab is speech directed to someone capable of understanding, in a form that conveys the intended meaning, such as direct address with anta.
rows.anchor: والخطاب توجيه الكلام إلى مدرك له بصيغة منبئة عن المراد

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says creatures cannot speak to the Lord without His permission.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل لا يقدر الخلق على أن يكلموا الرب إلا بإذنه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: The fifth reported view identifies the Spirit as human beings; standing in a row means standing in ordered ranks.
rows.anchor: وخامسها: أن الروح بنو آدم عن الحسن وقوله صفا معناه مصطفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those permitted to speak are believers and angels, and the sound word they said in earthly life was the testimony of divine unity.
rows.anchor: { لا يتكلمون إلا من أذن له الرحمن } وهم المؤمنون والملائكة { وقال } في الدنيا { صوابا } أي شهد بالتوحيد وقال: لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: الحسن والكلبي
rows.claim: They interpret speaking as intercession: none intercedes except one whom the Merciful permits to intercede.
rows.anchor: إن الكلام ها هنا الشفاعة أي لا يشفعون إلا لمن أذن له الرحمن أن يشفع عن الحسن والكلبي

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Abu Abdillah says the permitted speakers are the Imams: they glorify God, bless the Prophet, and intercede for their followers, and God does not refuse them; al-Ayyashi transmits the report mursal.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عبد الله ع قال: سئل عن هذه الآية فقال: نحن والله المأذون لهم يوم القيامة والقائلون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The true day is the Resurrection, whose occurrence is certain and beyond doubt.
rows.anchor: { ذلك اليوم الحق } الذي لا شك في كونه وحصوله يعني القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever chooses can make a return to God through obedience and righteous action; excuses have been removed, paths clarified, and messengers delivered their message.
rows.anchor: فمن شاء عمل عملا صالحا يؤوب إلى ربه فقد أزيحت العلل وأوضحت السبل وبلغت الرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ma'ab is a place or means of return, derived from awb; Ubayd's couplet uses the verb for returning from absence.
rows.anchor: والمآب مفعل من الأوب وهو الرجوع قال عبيد: وكل ذي غيبة يؤوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threatened near punishment is the hereafter, since anything that is coming is near.
rows.anchor: { إنا أنذرناكم عذابا قريبا } يعني العذاب في الآخرة فإن كل ما هو آت قريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person awaits the recompense for what he sent ahead: obedience brings reward and sin brings punishment.
rows.anchor: ينتظر جزاء ما قدمه فإن قدم الطاعة انتظر الثواب وإن قدم المعصية انتظر العقاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, each person sees good and evil deeds fixed in the record, hoping for reward for good and fearing punishment for evil.
rows.anchor: كل أحد ينظر إلى عمله في ذلك اليوم من خير وشر مثبتا عليه في صحيفته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbeliever wishes he had been dust so he would not be resurrected or judged and could escape that day's punishment; al-Zajjaj glosses it as wishing he had never been raised.
rows.anchor: ليتمنى أن لو كان ترابا لا يعاد ولا يحاسب ليتخلص من عقاب ذلك اليوم

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar reports that the earth is spread out and beasts are gathered, then a hornless sheep receives retaliation from the horned sheep that gored it.
rows.anchor: مدت الأرض مد الأديم وحشر الدواب والبهائم والوحوش ثم يجعل القصاص بين الدواب حتى يقتص للشاة الجماء من الشاة القرناء

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the animal that was gored receives retaliation from the animal that gored it.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: يقاد يوم القيامة للمنطوحة من الناطحة

rows.speaker: المقاتلان
rows.claim: The two Muqatils say all creatures other than humans and jinn are gathered, questioned, and given just recompense; after they are told to return to their former state they become dust, and the unbeliever wishes for that state.
rows.anchor: إن الله يجمع الوحوش والهوام والطير وكل شيء غير الثقلين فيقول من ربكم فيقولون الرحمن الرحيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view identifies the unbeliever as Iblis, who mocked Adam's origin in clay and boasted of fire, then wishes he were dust when he sees Adam's and the believers' honor.
rows.anchor: المراد بالكافر هنا إبليس عاب آدم بأن خلق من تراب وافتخر بالنار

rows.speaker: أهل الحجاز والبصرة
rows.claim: The Hijaz and Basra readers recite Tuwa without tanwin, while the other readers give it tanwin.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل الحجاز والبصرة طوى بغير تنوين والباقون بالتنوين

rows.speaker: أهل الحجاز وعباس ويعقوب
rows.claim: These readers recite tazakka with a doubled z; the other readers use the lighter form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أهل الحجاز وعباس ويعقوب تزكى بتشديد الزاء والباقون بتخفيفها

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda says non-nunated Tuwa is a feminine proper name, while the nunated form is like thuna, meaning sanctified repeatedly.
rows.anchor: طوى مضمومة الأول ومكسورته فمن لم ينون جعله اسما مؤنثا ومن نون جعله مثل ثنى على معنى المقدس مرة بعد مرة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan read Tuwa with a kasra on the first letter and explained it as blessed and sanctified twice; Tarafa's line supports the sense of repetition in ṭawā.
rows.anchor: روي عن الحسن أنه قرأ طوى بكسر الطاء وقال وطوي بالبركة والتقديس مرتين

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali says an uninflected Tuwa could be a town or place name, or a verbal noun patterned like Zafar or Mamar; an inflected form could likewise be a place name or a proper name like Zuhal, Hatam, and Lakaa.
rows.anchor: أنه جعله اسم بلدة أو بقعة أو يكون معولا كزفر وممر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tazakka means purifying oneself from unbelief; an omitted noun is understood, as in asking whether the addressee has a wish or need for it.
rows.anchor: { تزكى } معناه تطهر من الكفر والمبتدأ محذوف من اللفظ مراد في المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The light form is understood as tatazakka with its initial ta deleted; the doubled reading assimilates that ta into z because the sounds are close.
rows.anchor: ومن قال تزكى أراد تتزكى فأدغم تاء التفعل في الزاء لتقاربهما ومن خفف حذف التاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about Moses is a reportive question, and divine calling means summoning him with direct address.
rows.anchor: { هل أتاك } يامحمد { حديث موسى } استفهام يراد به التقرير

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: Mujahid and Qatada identify Tuwa as the name of a valley; another explanation derives the name from being sanctified twice, the place where God spoke with Moses.
rows.anchor: { طوى } اسم واد عن مجاهد وقتادة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh had risen in arrogance, disbelieved in God, and exceeded proper bounds in rebellion and corruption.
rows.anchor: { اذهب إلى فرعون إنه طغى } أي علا وتكبر وكفر بالله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Moses' polite invitation asks Pharaoh to purify himself from idolatry and testify that there is no god but God.
rows.anchor: { فقل هل لك إلى أن تزكى } أي تتطهر من الشرك وتشهد أن لا إله إلا الله عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The invitation can also mean asking whether Pharaoh wants to accept Islam, reform, and purify himself.
rows.anchor: هل لك رغبة إلى أن تسلم وتصلح وتطهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guiding Pharaoh to his Lord can mean teaching him to know his Creator and Sustainer, or guiding him to the path of God's approval and reward.
rows.anchor: { وأهديك إلى ربك } أي وأدلك إلى معرفة ربك وأنه خلقك ورباك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The result of that guidance is fear of God and leaving what He prohibited; the narrative omits the step that Moses went to Pharaoh and called him.
rows.anchor: { فتخشى } أي فتخافه فتفارق ما نهاك عنه وفي الكلام حذف تقديره فأتاه ودعاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The greatest sign shown to Pharaoh is the staff.
rows.anchor: { فأراه الآية الكبرى } يعني العصا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan identifies the greatest sign as Moses' shining hand.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: هي اليد البيضاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh denied that the sign came from God, disobeyed God's prophet, and rejected his prophethood.
rows.anchor: { فكذب } بأنها من الله { وعصى } نبي الله وجحد نبوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh turned away to find something that could defeat Moses' great proof, but only increased in error.
rows.anchor: { ثم أدبر } فرعون أي ولى الدبر ليطلب ما يكسر به حجة موسى في المعجزة العظيمة

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i says Pharaoh fled after seeing the huge serpent because he was afraid of it.
rows.anchor: لما رأى الحية في عظمها خاف منها فأدبر وسعى هربا عن الجبائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word yas'a means that Pharaoh worked corruption in the land.
rows.anchor: { يسعى } أي يعمل بالفساد في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh gathered his people and soldiers and called out to them.
rows.anchor: { فحشر } أي فجمع قومه وجنوده { فنادى } فيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's boast means that he claimed there was no lord above him.
rows.anchor: { فقال أنا ربكم الأعلى } أي لا رب فوقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun loses its light and then disperses, in a sequence compared with the scattering of the stars.
rows.anchor: يذهب ضوؤها ثم تتناثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ʿishar are camels pregnant for ten months; after giving birth they can still be called ʿishar, and they are the Arabs' most prized property, now left without a herdsman.
rows.anchor: النوق الحوامل أتت عليها عشرة أشهر وبعد الوضع تسمى عشارا أيضا وهي أنفس مال عند العرب

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i, as related from Abu Amr, interprets the ʿishar as clouds that cease to rain; al-Azhari says he does not know this usage in Arabic.
rows.anchor: وقيل: العشار السحاب تعطل فلا تمطر عن الجبائي وحكي ذلك عن أبي عمرو قال الأزهري: لا أعرف هذا في اللغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wild beasts are gathered for mutual redress; God gives them compensation for the pains they suffered, then they either remain blessed forever or, in other views, are later returned to dust.
rows.anchor: يحشر الله سبحانه الوحوش ليوصل إليها ما تستحقه من الأعواض على الآلام التي نالتها في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who say compensation is everlasting have the beasts remain blessed forever; some say God perpetuates it as a favor to prevent grief, while others say He turns them to dust after they receive it.
rows.anchor: فمن قال إن العوض دائم تبقى منعمة إلى الأبد ومن قال: تستحق العوض منقطعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seas are mixed, their fresh and salt waters pouring into one another until they are full.
rows.anchor: { وإذا البحار سجرت } أي أرسل عذبها على مالحها ومالحها على عذبها حتى امتلأت

rows.speaker: مجاهد ومقاتل والضحاك
rows.claim: Mujahid, Muqatil, and al-Dahhak say the seas burst into one another and become a single sea as the barrier is lifted.
rows.anchor: فجر بعضها في بعض فصارت البحور كلها بحرا واحدا ويرتفع البرزخ عن مجاهد ومقاتل والضحاك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the seas are ignited and become raging fire.
rows.anchor: سجرت أي أوقدت فصارت نارا تضطرم عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: Hasan and Qatada say the seas dry up and not a drop of water remains.
rows.anchor: يبست وذهب ماؤها فلم يبق فيها قطرة عن الحسن وقتادة

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i takes the seas to be the seas of Hell, filled with pus and fluid from the bodies of its inhabitants, since the seas of this world have perished.
rows.anchor: ملئت من القيح والصديد الذي يسيل من أبدان أهل النار في النار وأراد بحار جهنم

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب وابن عباس ومجاهد والحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: They say each person is paired with a counterpart, with the people of Hell paired with their kind and the people of Paradise with theirs.
rows.anchor: قرن كل إنسان بشكله من أهل النار وبشكله من أهل الجنة

rows.speaker: عكرمة والشعبي وأبو مسلم
rows.claim: They interpret the pairing as spirits being returned to bodies so people become alive again.
rows.anchor: ردت الأرواح إلى الأجساد فتصير أحياء عن عكرمة والشعبي وأبي مسلم

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i says a misguided person is paired with the human or demon who led him astray.
rows.anchor: يقرن الغاوي بمن أغواه من إنسان أو شيطان عن الجبائي

rows.speaker: عطاء ومقاتل
rows.claim: Ata and Muqatil say righteous believers are paired with houris and unbelievers with devils.
rows.anchor: قرنت نفوس الصالحين من المؤمنين بالحور العين وقرنت نفوس الكافرين بالشياطين عن عطاء ومقاتل

rows.speaker: أهل الكوفة وأبو جعفر
rows.claim: The Kufan readers and Abu Ja'far use the light reading of fa-ʿadalaka; the other readers double the d, yielding the sense that God shaped the creature's form.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة وأبو جعفر فعدلك خفيفة والباقون بالتشديد

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Ja'far reads yukadhdhibun with a y, making the clause report what unbelievers do; the other readers address them with t.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر بل يكذبون بالياء والباقون بالتاء

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأهل البصرة
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir and Basra readers raise yawm, while the other readers put it in the accusative.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأهل البصرة { يوم لا تملك } بالرفع والباقون بالنصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The raised reading makes the phrase a predicate of an omitted huwa: Judgment Day is the day when no soul controls anything for another.
rows.anchor: قوله { يوم لا تملك نفس } أنه خبر مبتدأ محذوف أي هو يوم لا تملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative can treat the phrase as the predicate of an implied recompense, since the preceding mention of Judgment Day supplies that event; it can also retain the usual adverbial accusative for a time expression.
rows.anchor: وأما النصب فإنه لما قال { وما أدراك ما يوم الدين } فجرى ذكر الدين وهو الجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative is supported by comparable time expressions in other verses; Abu al-Hasan says raising those examples is also good, but prefers the community's established reading.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الحسن: ولو رفع ذلك كله كان جيدا إلا أنا نختار ما عليه الناس

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: In a noncanonical reading Sa'id ibn Jubayr reads ma agharraka bi-rabbika, which may ask what caused the person to be deceived or express astonishment.
rows.anchor: وفي الشواذ قراءة سعيد بن جبير ما أغرك بربك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression can also be understood as an exclamation, as can the wording in the cited verse about people being patient over the Fire.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون تعجبا وقد قيل في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A lexical derivation from ghirr or gharara yields the sense how ignorant or heedless you are; deriving it from ghurur is also possible but irregular, as in the cited idiom.
rows.anchor: وأغرك يجوز أن يكون من الغر والغرارة فيكون معناه ما أجهلك وما أغفلك عما يراد بك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Infitar, in-shiqaq, and in-sidaʿ are near synonyms; intithar is the falling of something in multiple directions, while tafjir is the repeated opening of water channels into each other.
rows.anchor: الانفطار والانشقاق والانصداع نظائر والانتثار تساقط الشيء في الجهات والتفجير خرق بعض مواضع الماء إلى بعض على التكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fujur is linked linguistically to breaking out through many sins, and fajr to the breaking forth of light.
rows.anchor: ومنه الفجور لانخراق صاحبه بالخروج إلى كثير من الذنوب ومنه الفجر لانفجاره بالضياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baʿthara and baḥthara describe turning a basin's bottom to the top and bringing what was inside outward; ghurur is an appearance that falsely makes one feel safe from danger through ignorance.
rows.anchor: بعثرت الحوض وبحثرته إذا جعلت أسفله أعلاه والبعثرة والبحثرة إثارة الشيء بقلب باطنه إلى ظاهره

rows.speaker: الحرث بن حلزة
rows.claim: Al-Harith ibn Hilliza's line says they did not deceive you, illustrating the word gharur.
rows.anchor: لم يغروكم غرورا ولكن رفع الآل جمعهم والضحاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In one grammatical analysis, ma is emphatic and the meaning is that God formed the person in whichever form He chose, tall, short, or otherwise; rakabaka is coordinated with ʿadalaka with a conjunction omitted.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن تكون ما مزيدة مؤكدة والمعنى في أي صورة شاء ركبك إما طويلا وإما قصيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, ma is conditional: God formed the person in whatever form He wished; the interrogative phrase must attach to an omitted verb, not rakabaka or ʿadalaka, following Sibawayhi's rule about moving an object before a conditional clause.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون ما في معنى الشرط والجزاء فيكون المعنى في أي صورة ما شاء أن يركبك فيها ركبك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaslawna can be accusative as a circumstantial phrase or nominative as a second predicate, meaning that the wicked are in Hell, burning there.
rows.anchor: يصلونها في موضع نصب على الحال ويجوز أن يكون في موضع رفع فيكون خبرا لأنه خبر بعد خبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky splits apart, as in the verse describing the sky splitting with clouds.
rows.anchor: { إذا السماء انفطرت } أي انشقت وتقطعت

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the stars fall black and without light.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: سقطت سودا لا ضوء لها

rows.speaker: قتادة والجبائي
rows.claim: Qatada and al-Jubba'i say the seas burst into each other, fresh water into salt and salt into fresh, and become a single sea.
rows.anchor: فتح بعضها في بعض عذبها في ملحها وملحها في عذبها فصارت بحرا واحدا عن قتادة والجبائي

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan alternatively says the sea water disappears.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه ذهب ماؤها عن الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The graves are overturned and their dead raised; alternatively, they are searched to bring the dead out at resurrection.
rows.anchor: قلب ترابها وبعث الموتى الذين فيها. وقيل: معناه بحثت عن الموتى فأخرجوا منها يريد عند البعث عن ابن عباس ومقاتل

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud says what is sent ahead includes good and evil deeds, while what is left behind includes a good or bad practice that others follow, with their reward or burden added to its originator's.
rows.anchor: ما قدمت من خير أو شر وما أخرت من سنة حسنة أستن بها بعده فله أجر من اتبعه

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet teaches that whoever establishes a good practice receives its reward and the reward of those who follow it, while whoever establishes an evil practice bears its burden and theirs without reducing theirs.
rows.anchor: فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: When the Prophet recited the question about what deludes a person from his Lord, he answered that ignorance had deluded him.
rows.anchor:
النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لما تلا هذه الآية قال:
" غره جهله "

rows.speaker: حذيفة بن اليمان
rows.claim: After a man gave charity and others followed, Hudhayfa recited this verse.
rows.anchor: قال فتلا حذيفة بن اليمان { علمت نفس ما قدمت وأخرت }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse asks what deceived a person about his Creator and made him follow falsehood and disobey.
rows.anchor: أي أي شيء غرك بخالقك وخدعك وسول لك الباطل حتى عصيته وخالفته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Karim may mean the benefactor whose actions are pure generosity, with no pursuit of gain or defense against harm.
rows.anchor: هو المنعم الذي كل أفعاله إحسان وإنعام لا يجر به نفعا ولا يدفع به ضررا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another definition of al-Karim is one who gives what is due and beyond what is due without demanding what is owed to him.
rows.anchor: هو الذي يعطي من عليه وما ليس عليه ولا يطلب ماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another definition says the Generous accepts a little and gives much.
rows.anchor: هو الذي يقبل اليسير ويعطي الكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further sign of God's generosity is that He does more than forgive sins: He changes them into good deeds.
rows.anchor: من كرمه سبحانه أنه لم يرض بالعفو عن السيئات حتى بدلها بالحسنات

rows.speaker: الفضيل بن عياض
rows.claim: Asked what he would answer God, Fudayl says he would say that God's lowered veils had deceived him.
rows.anchor: قال أقول غرني ستورك المرخاة

rows.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
rows.claim: Yahya ibn Mu'adh says he would answer that God's past and present kindness had deceived him.
rows.anchor: قلت غرني بك برك بي سالفا وآنفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other answers say that God's forbearance or the generosity of the Generous was what deceived the speaker.
rows.anchor: وعن بعضهم قال غرني حلمك وعن أبي بكر الوراق غرني كرم الكريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse names God al-Karim rather than another attribute as if prompting the reply that the Generous One's generosity was what deceived the person.
rows.anchor: وإنما قال سبحانه الكريم دون سائر أسمائه وصفاته لأنه كأنه لقنه الإجابة

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud says everyone will meet God alone on Resurrection Day and be asked what deceived him and what he did and answered the messengers.
rows.anchor: ما منكم من أحد إلا سيخلو الله به يوم القيامة فيقول يا بن آدم ما غرك بي

rows.speaker: أمير المؤمنين
rows.claim: Ali warns that many are deluded by God's concealment of their faults and gradually drawn in by His favors.
rows.anchor: كم مغرور بالستر عليه ومستدرج بالإحسان إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created the human from a drop when he was nothing, then formed him into a hearing, seeing person and made him balanced.
rows.anchor: { الذي خلقك } من نطفة ولم تك شيئا { فسواك } إنسانا تسمع وتبصر { فعدلك } أي جعلك معتدلا

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil explains that God proportioned the person's two eyes, ears, hands, and feet, with neither of each pair out of balance with its counterpart.
rows.anchor: عدل خلقك في العينين والأذنين واليدين والرجلين عن مقاتل

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: In a report transmitted through al-Rida and his forefathers, the Prophet tells a man that the child may resemble any lineage between the sperm and Adam, in accordance with God's forming in whatever image He wills.
rows.anchor: " عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال لرجل:

rows.speaker: عكرمة وأبو صالح
rows.claim: Ikrima and Abu Salih say God may form a person in any created shape, even a human, donkey, or ape.
rows.anchor: في أي صورة ما شاء من صور الخلق ركبك إن شاء في صورة إنسان وإن شاء في صورة حمار وإن شاء في صورة قرد عن عكرمة وأبي صالح

rows.speaker: الصادق
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq says God could have formed a person differently but made him in the best form, unlike any animal.
rows.anchor: لو شاء ركبك على غير هذه الصورة والمعنى أنه سبحانه يقدر على جعلك كيف شاء ولكنه خلقك في أحسن تقويم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further interpretation lists possible forms by sex, build, beauty, and height: male or female, stout or thin, handsome or ugly, tall or short.
rows.anchor: في أي صورة شاء من ذكر أو أنثى أو جسيم أو نحيف حسن أو دميم طويل أو قصير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke rejects the claim that there is no resurrection or reckoning, since the proof is clear and this is no place for denial.
rows.anchor: ليس الأمر كما تزعمون أنه لا بعث ولا حساب وليس هنا موضع الإنكار للبعث مع وضوح الأمر

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: Mujahid and Qatada say the unbelievers deny the recompense because they deny resurrection and rising from the dead.
rows.anchor: { بل تكذبون } معاشر الكفار { بالدين } الذي هو الجزاء لإنكاركم البعث والنشور عن مجاهد وقتادة

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i interprets the denied din as the religion brought by Muhammad, Islam.
rows.anchor: وقيل: تكذبون بالدين الذي جاء به محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو الإسلام عن الجبائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guardian angels record human acts of obedience and sin.
rows.anchor: { وإن عليكم لحافظين } من الملائكة يحفظون عليكم ما تعلمونه من الطاعات والمعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guardian angels are honored by their Lord and write people's deeds; nothing they do is hidden from the angels.
rows.anchor: { كراما } على ربهم { كاتبين } يكتبون أعمال بني آدم { يعلمون ما تفعلون } من خير وشر فيكتبونه عليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says angels know what a person does necessarily, while another says they know by inference.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن الملائكة تعلم ما يفعله العبد إما باضطرار وإما باستدلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view limits their knowledge to outward acts; Tabarsi says that view implies human beings originate their acts, since otherwise the statement that they do them would not be sound.
rows.anchor: يعلمون ما تفعلون من الله دون الباطن وفي هذا دلالة على أن أفعال العبد حادثة من جهتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The righteous are God's obedient allies in this life and will be in Paradise.
rows.anchor: { إن الأبرار لفي نعيم } وهو الجنة والأبرار أولياء الله المطيعون في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wicked in this passage are unbelievers who deny the Prophet; they are fixed in Hell and never absent from it.
rows.anchor: { وإن الفجار لفي جحيم } وهو العظيم من النار والمراد بالفجار هنا الكفار المكذبون للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelievers remain in Hell perpetually and are never absent from it.
rows.anchor: { وما هم عنها بغائبين } أي لا يكونون غائبين عنها بل يكونون مؤبدين فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Major sinners among Muslims are not eternally in Hell; the context identifies the wicked as unbelievers, so the verse cannot prove the eternal-threat position when that contextual restriction is plausible.
rows.anchor: وقد دل الدليل على أن أهل الكبيرة من المسلمين لا يخلدون في النار ولأنه سبحانه قد ذكر المكذبين بالدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the question about Judgment Day magnifies its severity and draws attention to its many terrors.
rows.anchor: تعظيما له لشدته وتنبيها على عظم حاله وكثرة أهواله

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i says the repeated question can ask what bliss the people of Paradise and punishment the people of Hell will find on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أراد ما أدراك ما في يوم الدين من النعيم لأهل الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one can defend another who deserves punishment, as people can often protect one another in worldly life.
rows.anchor: لا يملك أحد الدفاع عن غيره ممن يستحق العقاب كما يملك كثير من الناس في دار الدنيا ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that day, judgment belongs to God alone, including recompense, reward, pardon, and punishment.
rows.anchor: { والأمر يومئذ لله } وحده أي الحكم له في الجزاء والثواب والعفو والانتقام

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Ja'far says that all authority is God's even now; on Resurrection Day rulers perish and no ruler remains but God.
rows.anchor: عن أبي جعفر ع أنه قال: إن الأمر يومئذ واليوم كله لله يا جابر إذا كان يوم القيامة بادت الحكام

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says the day is one when no soul can provide another unbelieving soul any benefit.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه يوم لا تملك نفس لنفس كافرة شيئا من المنفعة عن مقاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God had granted many people powers and judgments in worldly life, but in the Resurrection no command or rule belongs to anyone else.
rows.anchor: قد ملك في الدنيا كثيرا من الناس أمورا وأحكاما وفي القيامة لا أمر لسواه ولا حكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's intercession remains possible because it occurs only by God's command and permission and is part of His own governance.
rows.anchor: أن ذلك لا يكون إلا بأمره تعالى وبإذنه وهو من تدابيره
